 Order

By the present appeal filed under Section 374(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the appellants have challenged the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 03.04.2007 passed by Additional Sessions Judge, Fast Track Court, Amarpatan District Satna in S.T. No.137/2006 whereby the appellant No. 1 and 2 have been convicted under Section 498A of Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 2 years and fine of Rs.300/- for the offence and RI for 1 year and fine of Rs.200/- respectively each and in default, to further undergo RI for one-one months each.
2 .

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: As none appeared on behalf of the appellants, Shri K. Noor Fakhruddin, Advocate who is present in the court, has been requested to assist the Court on behalf of the appellants as amicus curiae.
3 . The learned counsel for the appellants has submitted that the prosecution failed to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt.
During the trial, the appellants namely, Rajbhan Loni remain in custody from 01.05.2006 to 26.07.2006 and appellant Kallubai Loni 01.05.2006 to 06.07.2006.
The incident was of the year 2006 and taken place all of a sudden in heat of passion.

1 rea behind the incident so a liberal view on the point of sentence be taken by the Court, so he prayed that the sentence be reduced to period already undergone.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4 . Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent/State supported the judgment and submitted that the prosecution has duly proved the incident and the learned sessions Court has rightly convicted the appellants under Section 498A of Indian Penal Code.
He said that Court is at liberty to consider the case on the point of sentence.

5. After considering the arguments of both the parties and after perusal of record, it appears that FIR was lodged at P.S. Amarpatan on 16.04.2006 against the appellants which was registered as Crime No.133/2006 under Sections 498A, 306, 34 of the IPC.
After investigation, the charge-sheet was filed.

6. Learned Trial Judge after considering the statements of the witnesses by judgment dated 03.04.2007 convicted the appellants under Section 498A of the IPC and sentenced as stated herein above, however, the findings recorded by the learned Trial Judge are based on due appreciation of evidence and do not require any interference.
The judgment of conviction and conviction under Section under 498A of the IPC is upheld.

7. However, looking to the facts that the incident took place in the year 2006, the appellants namely Rajbhan Loni remain in custody from 01.05.2006 to 26.07.2006 and appellant Kallubai Loni 01.05.2006 to 06.07.2006, prosecution has not brought any past criminal antecedents of the appellants on record and there is no minimum sentence has been prescribed under Sections 498A of Indian Penal Code, I deem it proper to reduce the jail sentence of the appellants to the extent of the period which they have already undergone and accordingly, the jail sentence is reduced and the fine amount is maintained.
The appellants are on bail, their personal bonds and bail bonds be discharged.

Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed.
8.
Record of the trial Court be sent back along with copy of the judgment.
